Atari games

Every program reads the 128-byte console RAM, never pixels, and contains no learned weights. Breakout, Ms. Pac-Man, Montezuma's Revenge and Space Invaders are the sticky-action champions (each step repeats the previous action with probability 0.25). The RAM layout is not given to the improvers: each program decoded it by probing the emulator.

Breakout · sticky actions

sticky-action champion, generation 3 (Codex) · sticky test 788 (start 473) · without sticky its predecessor reached the maximum 864 · 325 lines of Python

  • Decodes the paddle, ball, score, lives and the full 6 × 18 brick wall from RAM bit masks, and found the ball's velocity stored in RAM as signed fixed-point numbers.
  • Wrote the paddle's lagged motion as an exact per-frame rule and simulates the ball frame by frame, including wall bounces and brick breaks.
  • Breaks endless loops in stages: jitters its aim, meets the ball late, detects an exactly repeating bounce cycle and taps the paddle to escape it, and finally drops a ball if it has a spare life.
  • For sticky actions it plans by search over two-part move sequences and scores each one under nine delay scenarios: zero, one or two lost frames at the first and at later action changes, weighted by how likely each is.
  • It prefers to arrive early and penalises every extra action change, since each change is another chance for a sticky repeat to cost a frame; it stopped steering the ball toward bricks, which hurt under sticky actions.

def _simulate_paddle(self, r, px):
    """Paddle x at every future frame (0..4H) for every plan -> (P, 4H+1), plus the
    controller travel wasted inside the wall dead zones per plan."""
    P, H = self.plans.shape
    # Delays at the first and subsequent changes are independent. This
    # captures, for example, a late start followed by an immediate stop.
    plans = np.tile(self.plans, (9, 1))
    first_delays = np.repeat(np.repeat(np.arange(3), 3), P)
    later_delays = np.repeat(np.tile(np.arange(3), 3), P)
    pos = np.empty((9 * P, 4 * H + 1))
    rr = np.full(9 * P, float(r))
    pp = np.full(9 * P, float(px))
    pos[:, 0] = pp
    dead = np.zeros(9 * P)
    lo_r, hi_r = R_C - P_MAX, R_C - P_MIN
    previous = np.full(9 * P, self.last_move)
    changed = np.zeros(9 * P, dtype=bool)
    for t in range(H):
        current = plans[:, t]
        delays = np.where(changed, later_delays, first_delays)
        changed |= current != previous
        for i in range(4):
            move = np.where(i < delays, previous, current)
            pp = np.clip(np.ceil((pp + R_C - rr) / 2.0), P_MIN, P_MAX)
            rr = np.clip(rr - R_FRAME * move, R_MIN, R_MAX)
            pos[:, 4 * t + i + 1] = pp
        previous = current
        dead += np.maximum(0.0, lo_r - rr) + np.maximum(0.0, rr - hi_r)
    return pos, dead

"""Breakout RAM policy: predict where the ball meets the paddle and plan paddle moves to be there.

RAM map (probed, see NOTES.md):
  ram[57]  lives
  ram[70]  paddle controller value r (0..184). Per frame: RIGHT r -= ~5.6, LEFT r += ~5.6, clipped.
  ram[72]  drawn paddle x px (55..191). Per frame (exact):
           px' = clip(ceil((px + 234 - r) / 2), 55, 191)
  ram[76], ram[77] score (hundreds; BCD tens/ones)
  ram[99]  ball x (walls at ~55 and ~201)
  ram[101] ball y (grows downward; 0 = no ball in play)
  ram[103:105] vertical velocity as signed 8.8 fixed point
  ram[105:107] negated horizontal velocity as signed 8.8 fixed point
  ram[108] half paddle width w (8 normal; 6 after the paddle shrinks)
Actions: 0 NOOP, 1 FIRE, 2 RIGHT, 3 LEFT. One agent step = 4 frames.

Hit rule (fit with 0 errors on ~6000 frame-level contacts): the ball is returned iff on some
frame with ball y in [177, 183], (ball_x - paddle_x) is in [1, 2w+1]. Offsets in [1, w] send
the ball left, [w+1, 2w+1] send it right.

Each step:
  1. simulate the ball (walls + bricks) until it passes the paddle band;
  2. enumerate short paddle action sequences under several sticky-action delays;
  3. select a safe interception, preferring early, steady movement.
If no brick is scored for a long time, perturb the aim point and finally drop the ball on
purpose (a fresh life restarts the ball slowly with new angles).
"""

import numpy as np

NOOP, FIRE, RIGHT, LEFT = 0, 1, 2, 3
S2A = {0: NOOP, 1: RIGHT, -1: LEFT}

# Brick (row, col) is present iff ram[base - row] & mask, with (base, mask) per column 0..17.
# Rows 0 (top, red) .. 5 (bottom, blue). Column c spans ball x ~[57+8c, 64+8c],
# row r spans ball y ~[49+6r, 54+6r].
BRICK_COLS = ([(35, 0xC0)]
              + [(29, m) for m in (0xC0, 0x30, 0x0C, 0x03)]
              + [(23, m) for m in (0x03, 0x0C, 0x30, 0xC0)]
              + [(17, m) for m in (0x30, 0xC0)]
              + [(11, m) for m in (0xC0, 0x30, 0x0C, 0x03)]
              + [(5, m) for m in (0x03, 0x0C, 0x30)])

# geometry / dynamics (probed)
Y_TOP = 23              # top wall (ball y at reversal)
Y_HIT, Y_BOT = 177, 183  # ball y range in which the paddle can return the ball
X_MIN, X_MAX = 55, 201  # ball x reflection bounds
P_MIN, P_MAX = 55, 191  # paddle x bounds
R_MIN, R_MAX = 0, 184   # controller bounds
R_FRAME = 5.6           # controller change per frame while moving
R_C = 234               # resting paddle x = R_C - r
# planning
HORIZON = 10            # planning horizon in steps
OFF_D = 1               # default aim: ball_x - paddle_x = w + OFF_D (centre of the hit window)
SAFE = 5                # wanted margin (px) inside the hit window
PEN = 10.0              # cost per px of missing margin
DEAD_PEN = 0.02         # cost per unit of controller travel inside a wall dead zone (per step)
SIM_FRAMES = 400        # max frames of ball flight to simulate
DELAY_WEIGHTS = np.array([.75, .1875, .0625])
SCENARIO_WEIGHTS = np.outer(DELAY_WEIGHTS, DELAY_WEIGHTS).reshape(-1)
# stall breaking
STALL = 400             # steps without scoring before perturbing the aim point
JIT_EDGE = 3            # keep the jittered aim at least this far from the window edges
STALL2 = 3000           # steps without scoring before dropping, if another life remains


def ball_step(x, y, fx, fy):
    """Advance the ball one frame, reflecting off the side and top walls."""
    x += fx
    y += fy
    if x < X_MIN:
        x, fx = 2 * X_MIN - x, -fx
    elif x > X_MAX:
        x, fx = 2 * X_MAX - x, -fx
    if y < Y_TOP:
        y, fy = 2 * Y_TOP - y, -fy
    return x, y, fx, fy


def brick_cell(x, y, fy):
    """(row, col) of the brick area the ball touches, or None (leading edge when descending)."""
    yy = y if fy < 0 else y + 3
    if 49 <= yy < 85:
        return int((yy - 49) // 6), min(17, max(0, int((x - 57) // 8)))
    return None


def read_bricks(ram):
    g = np.zeros((6, 18), dtype=bool)
    for c, (b, m) in enumerate(BRICK_COLS):
        for row in range(6):
            g[row, c] = bool(ram[b - row] & m)
    return g


def build_plans():
    """Candidate action sequences: s1 x n1, then s2 x n2, then NOOP -> (P, HORIZON)."""
    H = HORIZON
    plans = {tuple([s1] * n1 + [s2] * n2 + [0] * (H - n1 - n2))
             for s1 in (-1, 0, 1) for s2 in (-1, 0, 1)
             for n1 in range(H + 1) for n2 in range(H + 1 - n1)}
    return np.array(sorted(plans), dtype=np.float64)


class Policy:
    def __init__(self, spec: dict):
        self.plans = build_plans()
        self.reset()

    def reset(self) -> None:
        self.last_move = 0              # last requested paddle direction
        self.prev = None                # ball (x, y) at the previous step
        self.rng = np.random.default_rng(12345)
        self.last_score = 0
        self.lives = None
        self.since_score = 0            # steps since the score (or lives) last changed
        self.jitter = 0                 # stall breaker: shift of the aim point
        self.dropping = False           # stall breaker: losing the ball on purpose
        self.prev_vy_sign = 0
        self.loop_history = []
        self.escape_moves = []

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ main loop
    def act(self, obs, info: dict) -> int:
        action = self._act(obs, info)
        self.last_move = 1 if action == RIGHT else -1 if action == LEFT else 0
        return action

    def _act(self, obs, info: dict) -> int:
        ram = np.asarray(obs, dtype=np.int32)
        r, px, bx, by = int(ram[70]), int(ram[72]), int(ram[99]), int(ram[101])
        w = int(ram[108])
        prev = self.prev
        self.prev = (bx, by)

        vy_byte = int(ram[103])
        vy_sign = 0 if vy_byte == 0 else (1 if vy_byte < 128 else -1)
        returned = self.prev_vy_sign > 0 and vy_sign < 0 and by > 150
        self._update_stall(ram, prev, by, w, returned)
        self.prev_vy_sign = vy_sign
        if by == 0:
            self.dropping = False
            self.escape_moves.clear()
            return FIRE

        # Exact one- or two-return cycles can trap the ball indefinitely.
        # Pulse both directions to find a different controller position before
        # spending a life on a stall. Do not interrupt a deliberate drop.
        if self.since_score <= 2000:
            self.loop_history.clear()
        elif returned and (self.lives == 1 or self.since_score <= STALL2):
            signature = tuple(int(ram[i]) for i in (99, 100, 101, 102, 105, 106))
            self.loop_history.append(signature)
            self.loop_history = self.loop_history[-8:]
            if len(self.loop_history) == 8 and self.loop_history[2:] == self.loop_history[:-2]:
                direction = RIGHT if prev is not None and prev[0] - px > w else LEFT
                opposite = LEFT if direction == RIGHT else RIGHT
                self.escape_moves = [direction, NOOP, opposite, NOOP]
                self.loop_history.clear()
        if self.escape_moves:
            return self.escape_moves.pop(0)

        # long stall: the fast ball's paths form a closed lattice that misses the remaining
        # bricks; losing a life restarts the ball slowly with new angles and a full paddle.
        # Two cleared walls give the maximum 864 points; end that finished
        # game instead of spending the remaining episode on an empty board.
        if self.last_score >= 864 or (self.since_score > STALL2 and self.lives > 1):
            self.dropping = True
        # Ball velocities are stored as signed 8.8 fixed-point numbers;
        # horizontal RAM velocity has the opposite sign to the screen axis.
        vx_byte = int(ram[105])
        vx = -((vx_byte if vx_byte < 128 else vx_byte - 256) + int(ram[106]) / 256.0)
        vy = (vy_byte if vy_byte < 128 else vy_byte - 256) + int(ram[104]) / 256.0
        vel = (vx, vy) if 0 < abs(vy) <= 4 and abs(vx) <= 2 else None
        bricks = read_bricks(ram)
        sim = None if vel is None else self._sim_ball(bx, by, *vel, bricks)
        if self.dropping:
            # move the paddle to the wall farthest from where the ball will come down
            land = bx if sim is None else sim[0][0][1]
            return LEFT if land > 128 else RIGHT

        lo, hi = 1, 2 * w + 1               # hit window for (ball_x - paddle_x)
        aim = w + OFF_D + self.jitter
        pos, dead = self._simulate_paddle(r, px)
        if sim is None:
            return self._choose(self._goal_cost(pos, bx - aim), dead)
        band, out_vx = sim

        # On long scoreless loops, deliberately make the ball meet the paddle
        # later in the contact band. This shifts the next trajectory to a new lattice.
        late = (self.since_score > 1000 and len(band) > 1 and abs(out_vx) >= 1.5
                and P_MIN + hi + 2 <= band[0][1] <= P_MAX - 2)
        if late:
            aim = 0 if out_vx > 0 else hi + 1
        F = pos.shape[1] - 1
        if band[0][0] >= F:
            # ball is beyond the planning horizon: be at rest under its landing point
            return self._choose(self._goal_cost(pos, band[0][1] - aim), dead)
        js = np.array([j for j, _ in band if j <= F])
        xs = np.array([x for j, x in band if j <= F])
        if late:
            cost, m = self._contact_cost(pos, js, xs, lo, hi, aim, safe=1)
            if m >= 0.5:
                return self._choose(cost, dead)
            aim = w + OFF_D + self.jitter
        cost, _ = self._contact_cost(pos, js, xs, lo, hi, aim)
        return self._choose(cost, dead)

    def _update_stall(self, ram, prev, by, w, returned):
        """Count steps without scoring; once stalled, re-randomise the aim after each return."""
        score = int(ram[76]) * 100 + (int(ram[77]) >> 4) * 10 + (int(ram[77]) & 15)
        lives = int(ram[57])
        if lives != self.lives:
            self.lives = lives
            self.since_score = 0
        if score != self.last_score:
            self.last_score = score
            self.since_score = 0
            self.jitter = 0
        else:
            self.since_score += 1
        # On the second wall or in a prolonged stall, draw a single jitter
        # per bounce instead of redrawing on each ascending observation.
        if score >= 432 or self.since_score > 1000:
            just_returned = returned
        else:
            just_returned = prev is not None and prev[1] > by > 150
        if self.since_score > STALL and just_returned:
            lim = max(0, w - JIT_EDGE)
            self.jitter = int(self.rng.integers(-lim, lim + 1))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ paddle planning
    def _simulate_paddle(self, r, px):
        """Paddle x at every future frame (0..4H) for every plan -> (P, 4H+1), plus the
        controller travel wasted inside the wall dead zones per plan."""
        P, H = self.plans.shape
        # Delays at the first and subsequent changes are independent. This
        # captures, for example, a late start followed by an immediate stop.
        plans = np.tile(self.plans, (9, 1))
        first_delays = np.repeat(np.repeat(np.arange(3), 3), P)
        later_delays = np.repeat(np.tile(np.arange(3), 3), P)
        pos = np.empty((9 * P, 4 * H + 1))
        rr = np.full(9 * P, float(r))
        pp = np.full(9 * P, float(px))
        pos[:, 0] = pp
        dead = np.zeros(9 * P)
        lo_r, hi_r = R_C - P_MAX, R_C - P_MIN
        previous = np.full(9 * P, self.last_move)
        changed = np.zeros(9 * P, dtype=bool)
        for t in range(H):
            current = plans[:, t]
            delays = np.where(changed, later_delays, first_delays)
            changed |= current != previous
            for i in range(4):
                move = np.where(i < delays, previous, current)
                pp = np.clip(np.ceil((pp + R_C - rr) / 2.0), P_MIN, P_MAX)
                rr = np.clip(rr - R_FRAME * move, R_MIN, R_MAX)
                pos[:, 4 * t + i + 1] = pp
            previous = current
            dead += np.maximum(0.0, lo_r - rr) + np.maximum(0.0, rr - hi_r)
        return pos, dead

    @staticmethod
    def _goal_cost(pos, goal):
        """Ball still far away: be at the goal at the end of the horizon, at rest."""
        return np.abs(pos[:, -1] - goal) + 0.5 * np.abs(pos[:, 4::4] - goal).mean(axis=1)

    @staticmethod
    def _contact_cost(pos, js, xs, lo, hi, aim, safe=SAFE):
        """Cost the nominal catch and report the worst timing-shift margin.

        A catch can occur on any frame in the contact band. The worst margin
        across timing shifts is used to gate risky late-contact stall breaking.
        """
        F = pos.shape[1] - 1
        off = xs[None, :] - pos[:, js]
        nominal_m = np.minimum(off - lo, hi - off).max(axis=1)
        best_m = nominal_m
        for shift in (-1, 1):
            off = xs[None, :] - pos[:, np.clip(js + shift, 0, F)]
            margin = np.minimum(off - lo, hi - off).max(axis=1)
            best_m = np.minimum(best_m, margin)
        off0 = xs[0] - pos[:, js[0]]
        cost = PEN * np.maximum(0.0, safe - nominal_m) + np.abs(off0 - aim)
        # Move towards the interception point early, leaving time for the
        # paddle to settle and for sticky-action errors to be corrected.
        goal = xs[0] - aim
        cost += 0.5 * np.abs(pos[:, :int(js[0]) + 1:4] - goal).mean(axis=1)
        cost_by_scenario = cost.reshape(9, -1)
        margin_by_scenario = best_m.reshape(9, -1)
        aggregate = SCENARIO_WEIGHTS @ cost_by_scenario
        best = int(np.argmin(aggregate))
        return cost, float(np.min(margin_by_scenario[:, best]))

    def _choose(self, cost, dead):
        # Weight the delay scenarios and avoid wasted wall travel.
        cost = (cost + DEAD_PEN * dead).reshape(9, -1)
        cost = SCENARIO_WEIGHTS @ cost
        # Do not drive into a wall and reverse solely for a slightly better
        # final pixel: extra changes are unreliable with sticky actions.
        moves = np.abs(self.plans).sum(axis=1)
        reversals = (self.plans[:, 1:] * self.plans[:, :-1] < 0).sum(axis=1)
        cost += 1.0 * moves + 30.0 * reversals
        return S2A[int(self.plans[int(np.argmin(cost)), 0])]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ ball model
    @staticmethod
    def _sim_ball(x, y, fx, fy, bricks):
        """Frame-level ball flight (breaking bricks) until it passes the paddle band descending.
        Mutates the fresh brick map; returns ([(frame, x)] in the band, vx at contact) or None."""
        band = []
        if fy > 0 and Y_HIT <= y <= Y_BOT:
            band.append((0, float(x)))
        for j in range(1, SIM_FRAMES + 1):
            x, y, fx, fy = ball_step(x, y, fx, fy)
            cell = brick_cell(x, y, fy)
            if cell is not None and bricks[cell]:
                bricks[cell] = False
                fy = -fy
                continue
            if fy > 0 and y >= Y_HIT:
                if y > Y_BOT:
                    break
                band.append((j, x))
        return (band, fx) if band else None

Pong

generation 1 champion (Claude Code), without sticky actions · test 21, the maximum, on all 64 seeds · 15.8 with sticky actions · 230 lines of Python

  • Predicts where the ball crosses its paddle line, folding the path at the top and bottom walls.
  • Models its own sluggish paddle as a linear filter over recent inputs and refines the coefficients online by recursive least squares while playing.
  • Uses only the two steepest return angles and simulates the CPU paddle (at most 7 px per step) to pick the shot the CPU cannot reach.
  • Within 4 steps of contact it tries every sequence of up / down / stay through its paddle model.
  • Play is deterministic, so after 4 returns in one rally it randomises its shot to avoid endless loops.

dx, dy = vel
k = max(0, int(np.ceil((CONTACT_X - bx) / dx)))   # steps until contact
yc = reflect(by + dy * k)          # ball y on the contact frame
yn = reflect(by + dy * (k + 1))    # and one frame later
if self.plan_rel is None:
    self.rally += 1
    if self.rally > LOOP_AFTER:
        # long rally: the deterministic choice is probably looping
        ok = allowed_shots(yc)
        shot = ok[int(self.rng.integers(len(ok)))]
    else:
        _, cpu = run_ball_and_cpu(float(by), dy, float(o[50]), k)
        shot = choose_shot(yc, abs(dx), cpu)
    self.plan_rel = SHOTS[shot]

if k > HORIZON:
    return self.settle_toward(yc - self.plan_rel)
best, best_c = NOOP, None
for seq in SEQS[k + 1]:
    ps = self.simulate(seq)
    p1 = ps[-1]
    p0 = ps[-2] if k > 0 else self.last_p
    rel0, rel1 = yc - p0, yn - p1
    aim = 0.5 * (rel0 + rel1)
    c = (abs(aim - self.plan_rel) + VEL_PEN * abs(p1 - p0)
         + SAFE_PEN * (max(0.0, SAFE_LO - aim) + max(0.0, aim - SAFE_HI))
         + SAFE_PEN * sum(max(0.0, HIT_LO + 1.0 - r) + max(0.0, r - HIT_HI + 1.0)
                          for r in (rel0, rel1))
         + WALL_PEN * sum(max(0.0, PMIN + 4.0 - q) + max(0.0, q - PMAX + 4.0) for q in ps))
    if best_c is None or c < best_c - 1e-9:
        best, best_c = seq[0], c
return best

"""Pong RAM policy: model-predictive paddle aiming.

RAM layout (probed, see NOTES.md):
  ram[51] player (right) paddle y, ram[50] CPU paddle y,
  ram[49] ball x (increases toward us), ram[54] ball y (0 = no ball in play).
Actions: 0 NOOP, 2 up (y decreases), 3 down (y increases).

Paddle dynamics: UP/DOWN shift a hidden commanded position R by ~23 px; the
displayed paddle follows through a short linear filter.  A linear model
  dp[t+1] = sum_{i<4} c_i u[t-i] + sum_{j<3} d_j dp[t-j],   u = -1/0/+1
fits each episode to ~0.5 px, but the c coefficients depend on an
episode-specific frame phase, so they are refined online with recursive
least squares starting from a prior.

Hit geometry: rel = ball_y - paddle_y on the frame the ball reaches x>=186.
The ball is returned for rel in about [-3, 16]; outgoing dy is
-8 for rel<=0, -4 for 1..4, 0 for 5..8, +4 for 8..12, +8 for >=12.

Per point: wait near the centre, predict where the incoming ball crosses
CONTACT_X, pick a steep shot the CPU paddle cannot reach, then plan the last
few moves by brute-force search over action sequences with the paddle model.
"""

import itertools

import numpy as np

CONTACT_X = 186         # first ball x counted as "at our paddle"
CPU_X = 72              # ball x at which the CPU paddle meets it
TOP, BOTTOM = 45.0, 206.0   # ball y bounce limits
PMIN, PMAX = 38.0, 203.0    # paddle y limits
UP, DOWN, NOOP = 2, 3, 0
U = {NOOP: 0, UP: -1, DOWN: 1}
STEP = 23.0             # commanded-position shift per UP/DOWN

HIT_LO, HIT_HI = -3, 16     # rel window in which we return the ball
SAFE_LO, SAFE_HI = -1.0, 14.0
CPU_LO, CPU_HI = -2, 12     # CPU returns the ball for ball_y - cpu_y in this range
CPU_SPEED = 7.0             # CPU paddle max px/step
SHOTS = {-8: -1.0, 8: 14.0}   # outgoing dy -> rel to aim for (only steep shots beat the CPU)
WALL_MARGIN = 10.0          # keep the aimed paddle position this far from the walls
LOOP_AFTER = 4              # after this many returns in a rally, pick random shots

HORIZON = 4                 # MPC search when contact is at most this many steps away
SEQS = {k: list(itertools.product((NOOP, UP, DOWN), repeat=k)) for k in range(1, HORIZON + 2)}
VEL_PEN, SAFE_PEN, WALL_PEN = 0.25, 4.0, 2.0

NU, NV = 4, 3
PRIOR = np.array([7.5, 14.3, 7.7, 2.4, -0.34, -0.08, 0.05])
PRIOR_WEIGHT = 30.0


def reflect(y, lo=TOP, hi=BOTTOM):
    span = hi - lo
    p = (y - lo) % (2 * span)
    if p > span:
        p = 2 * span - p
    return lo + p


def run_ball_and_cpu(y, vy, c, n):
    """Advance ball y (bouncing) and the CPU paddle tracking it for n steps."""
    for _ in range(n):
        y_raw = y + vy
        if y_raw < TOP or y_raw > BOTTOM:
            vy = -vy
        y = reflect(y_raw)
        c += max(-CPU_SPEED, min(CPU_SPEED, y - c))
    return y, c


def eff_u(R, a):
    """Next commanded position and the effective (clamp-aware) input for action a."""
    Rn = min(max(R + STEP * U[a], PMIN), PMAX + 1)
    return Rn, (Rn - R) / STEP


def allowed_shots(yc):
    """Steep shots whose paddle position stays clear of the walls (model is poor there).

    Only dy = +-8 shots beat the CPU.  Since yc is in [TOP, BOTTOM], at least one of
    them is allowed except for a ball hugging the top wall, where -8 is the closest.
    """
    lo, hi = PMIN + WALL_MARGIN, PMAX - WALL_MARGIN
    return [s for s in (-8, 8) if lo <= yc - SHOTS[s] <= hi] or [-8]


def choose_shot(yc, dxa, cpu):
    """Pick the shot that leaves the CPU paddle farthest outside its return window."""
    n = max(1, int(round((CONTACT_X - CPU_X) / dxa)))
    best, best_m = None, -1e9
    for s in allowed_shots(yc):
        y, c = run_ball_and_cpu(yc, s, cpu, n)
        rel = y - c
        margin = max(CPU_LO - rel, rel - CPU_HI)
        if margin > best_m:
            best, best_m = s, margin
    return best


def ball_velocity(o, prev):
    if prev is None or o[54] == 0 or prev[54] == 0:
        return None
    dx = int(o[49]) - int(prev[49])
    dy = int(o[54]) - int(prev[54])
    if dx == 0 or abs(dx) > 12 or abs(dy) > 20:
        return None
    return dx, dy


class Policy:
    def __init__(self, spec: dict):
        self.rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
        self.reset()

    def reset(self) -> None:
        self.prev = None            # previous RAM
        self.plan_rel = None        # rel aimed for at the coming contact
        self.rally = 0              # returns in the current point
        self.us = [0.0] * NU        # recent effective inputs, most recent first
        self.dps = [0.0] * NV       # recent paddle steps, most recent first
        self.R = None               # estimated commanded position
        self.last_p = None
        self.last_feat = None
        self.theta = PRIOR.copy()   # RLS state
        self.P = np.eye(len(PRIOR)) / PRIOR_WEIGHT

    def act(self, obs, info: dict) -> int:
        o = obs.astype(np.int64)
        self.observe_paddle(float(o[51]))
        a = self.decide(o)
        self.R, u = eff_u(self.R, a)
        self.us = [u] + self.us[:-1]
        self.last_feat = np.array(self.us + self.dps)
        self.prev = o
        return a

    # ---- paddle model ----------------------------------------------------
    def observe_paddle(self, p):
        if self.last_p is None:
            self.last_p = p
            self.R = p + 1.0
            return
        dp = p - self.last_p
        # RLS update, away from the walls where the model does not hold
        if self.last_feat is not None and 50 < self.last_p < 192 and 50 < p < 192:
            x = self.last_feat
            Px = self.P @ x
            g = Px / (1.0 + x @ Px)
            self.theta = self.theta + g * (dp - x @ self.theta)
            self.P = self.P - np.outer(g, Px)
        self.dps = [dp] + self.dps[:-1]
        self.last_p = p
        # resync the command estimate when the paddle rests after NOOPs or sits at a wall
        if all(abs(d) < 0.5 for d in self.dps[:2]) and all(u == 0 for u in self.us[:3]):
            self.R = p + 1.0 if p > PMIN + 0.5 else PMIN
        if p <= PMIN + 0.5 and self.us[0] < 0:
            self.R = PMIN
        if p >= PMAX - 0.5 and self.us[0] > 0:
            self.R = PMAX + 1

    def simulate(self, seq):
        """Predicted paddle positions after each action of seq."""
        th = self.theta
        us, dps, p, R = list(self.us), list(self.dps), self.last_p, self.R
        ps = []
        for a in seq:
            R, u = eff_u(R, a)
            us = [u] + us[:-1]
            dp = float(np.dot(th[:NU], us) + np.dot(th[NU:], dps))
            p = min(max(p + dp, PMIN), PMAX)
            dps = [dp] + dps[:-1]
            ps.append(p)
        return ps

    # ---- control ---------------------------------------------------------
    def decide(self, o):
        bx, by = int(o[49]), int(o[54])
        vel = ball_velocity(o, self.prev)

        if by == 0:
            self.rally = 0
        if vel is None or vel[0] < 0 or bx > CONTACT_X + 4:
            # ball not coming at us: wait between the ball and the centre
            self.plan_rel = None
            target = 124.0 if by == 0 else 0.5 * (by + 124.0)
            return self.settle_toward(target - 6.0)

        dx, dy = vel
        k = max(0, int(np.ceil((CONTACT_X - bx) / dx)))   # steps until contact
        yc = reflect(by + dy * k)          # ball y on the contact frame
        yn = reflect(by + dy * (k + 1))    # and one frame later
        if self.plan_rel is None:
            self.rally += 1
            if self.rally > LOOP_AFTER:
                # long rally: the deterministic choice is probably looping
                ok = allowed_shots(yc)
                shot = ok[int(self.rng.integers(len(ok)))]
            else:
                _, cpu = run_ball_and_cpu(float(by), dy, float(o[50]), k)
                shot = choose_shot(yc, abs(dx), cpu)
            self.plan_rel = SHOTS[shot]

        if k > HORIZON:
            return self.settle_toward(yc - self.plan_rel)
        best, best_c = NOOP, None
        for seq in SEQS[k + 1]:
            ps = self.simulate(seq)
            p1 = ps[-1]
            p0 = ps[-2] if k > 0 else self.last_p
            rel0, rel1 = yc - p0, yn - p1
            aim = 0.5 * (rel0 + rel1)
            c = (abs(aim - self.plan_rel) + VEL_PEN * abs(p1 - p0)
                 + SAFE_PEN * (max(0.0, SAFE_LO - aim) + max(0.0, aim - SAFE_HI))
                 + SAFE_PEN * sum(max(0.0, HIT_LO + 1.0 - r) + max(0.0, r - HIT_HI + 1.0)
                                  for r in (rel0, rel1))
                 + WALL_PEN * sum(max(0.0, PMIN + 4.0 - q) + max(0.0, q - PMAX + 4.0) for q in ps))
            if best_c is None or c < best_c - 1e-9:
                best, best_c = seq[0], c
        return best

    def settle_toward(self, target):
        """Coarse move of the commanded position toward target (only if it gains > 2 px)."""
        target = min(max(target, PMIN + 8.0), PMAX - 8.0) + 1.0
        best, best_c = NOOP, abs(self.R - target)
        for a in (UP, DOWN):
            c = abs(eff_u(self.R, a)[0] - target)
            if c < best_c - 2.0:
                best, best_c = a, c
        return best

Ms. Pac-Man · sticky actions

sticky-action champion, generation 4 (Codex, after two Claude Code generations) · sticky test 38,306 (start 9,781; human 6,952) · 497 lines of Python

  • Built maps of all four mazes as graphs in RAM coordinates, with tunnels; the maze in play is read from RAM and reloaded on every board change.
  • Reads Ms. Pac-Man, the four ghosts, every pellet, the power pellets and the frightened timer from RAM, and does not count a ghost's returning eyes as danger.
  • Measures danger as corridor distance from the ghosts using each ghost's direction of travel, and routes to pellets with a cost that grows with the square of nearby danger; it saves power pellets until a ghost is close and chases frightened ghosts it can reach in time.
  • For sticky actions it checks every exit at a junction: an exit is safe only if it can reach open corridor while staying at least two steps ahead of every ghost, counting the slowdown from eating dots. If the planned exit is unsafe it re-plans among the safe ones.
  • It reverses at once from a head-on ghost and makes a second reversal soon after expensive, so a delayed input does not leave it dithering between two bad directions.

Key excerpt · policy.py lines 186–222. An exit is safe only if Ms. Pac-Man keeps a two-step lead over every ghost until open corridor.

def has_escape(self, start, q, cost, danger, powers=(), dots=(), pursued=False):
    """Can we get from start through exit q to a node no ghost reaches first?

    Our arrival time at each node must beat the ghost-distance estimate by
    ESCAPE_MARGIN. Normally an out-of-horizon node or ESCAPE_DEPTH steps
    of travel is enough; when pursued, require 20 steps of travel. A
    reachable power pellet also counts as an escape.
    """
    occupied = self.occupied
    if (start, q) in occupied:
        return False
    best = {start: 0.0}
    # Eating dots slows us down, so a following ghost gains on us.
    if q in dots:
        cost *= 1 + DOT_SLOW
    heap = [(cost, q)]
    while heap:
        t, p = heapq.heappop(heap)
        if t >= best.get(p, 1e9):
            continue
        g = danger.get(p)
        if g is not None and t + ESCAPE_MARGIN > g:
            continue
        best[p] = t
        # A close pursuer can follow through several turns, so look past
        # the first apparently clear node before calling that route safe.
        if ((g is None and not pursued) or t >= (20 if pursued else ESCAPE_DEPTH)
                or p in powers):
            return True
        for r, _, c in self.graph[p]:
            if (p, r) in occupied:
                continue
            if r in dots:
                c *= 1 + DOT_SLOW
            if t + c < best.get(r, 1e9):
                heapq.heappush(heap, (t + c, r))
    return False

"""Navigate the maze, collect pellets, and keep away from ghosts."""
import heapq
from maze import XS, YS, MAZES

# ALE minimal actions: right, left, down, up.
DIRS = {2:(1,0), 3:(-1,0), 4:(0,1), 1:(0,-1)}
REVERSE = {2:3, 3:2, 4:1, 1:4}
POWER_BITS = {(18,14):32, (158,14):8, (18,146):16, (158,146):4}
# Dot flags are arranged in three RAM bytes per horizontal row:
# x column -> (byte offset within the row, bit).
DOT_COLUMNS = {18:(0,64), 26:(1,128), 34:(1,32), 42:(1,8),
               50:(1,2), 58:(2,1), 66:(2,4), 74:(2,16),
               102:(1,16), 110:(1,4), 118:(1,1), 126:(2,2),
               134:(2,8), 142:(2,32), 150:(2,128), 158:(0,16)}

# Tuned for sticky actions (2026-11-04); see NOTES.md for rejected variants.
GHOST_REVERSE_PENALTY = 4.0   # extra steps for a ghost to reach the node behind it
GHOST_HORIZON = 22            # ghost-distance search is truncated here
RISK_RADIUS = 14              # ghost distances below this add risk
AVOID_COST = 25.0             # extra cost on power pellets being saved
POWER_TRIGGER = 20            # save power pellets while ghosts are this far
TURN_COST = 2.7
REV_COST = 1.5
REV_COOLDOWN = 14             # within this many steps of a reversal...
REV_COOLDOWN_COST = 10.0      # ...another reversal costs this much more
HUNT_MIN_TIMER = 6
HUNT_BUDGET = 0.5
FRUIT_EARLY = 15              # fruit pursuit range on maze types 0-1 (40 later)
# Escape check (2026-11-04, g002): only take exits that still have a way out.
ESCAPE_MARGIN = 2.0           # steps we must beat a ghost to a node by
ESCAPE_DEPTH = 12             # steps of safe travel that count as escaped
HOUSE_EXIT_Y = 70             # in-house ghosts above this y count as leaving
# Eating dots slows Pac-Man, which matters when a ghost is following.
DOT_SLOW = 0.2                # escape check: edges onto a dot take this much longer
OCCUPIED_COST = 40.0          # route cost of walking an edge into an oncoming ghost


def in_house(x, y):
    return 74 <= x <= 102 and 60 <= y <= 88

def on_screen(x, y):
    return 12 <= x <= 166 and 0 <= y <= 164

def frightened_timer(obs):
    return int(obs[116]) & 63

def ghost_pos(obs, j):
    return int(obs[6+j]), int(obs[12+j])

def is_frightened(obs, j):
    return bool(int(obs[1+j]) & 128)

def offsets(x, y, dx, dy, px, py):
    """Position of (px, py) along and across the direction (dx, dy) from (x, y)."""
    return (px-x)*dx + (py-y)*dy, abs((px-x)*dy - (py-y)*dx)


class Policy:
    def __init__(self, spec):
        self.load_maze(0)
        self.reset()

    def load_maze(self, maze_type):
        self.maze_type = maze_type
        rows, vertical, horizontal, tunnels = MAZES[maze_type]
        self.graph = {}
        self.pellet_bits = []
        for j, y in enumerate(YS):
            for i, x in enumerate(XS):
                if rows[j][i] == '#':
                    continue
                p = (x,y)
                if rows[j][i] == 'o' and p not in POWER_BITS:
                    offset, bit = DOT_COLUMNS[x]
                    self.pellet_bits.append((p, 59 + 3*j + offset, bit))
                edges = []
                for action, (di, dj) in DIRS.items():
                    ii, jj = i+di, j+dj
                    if not (0 <= ii < len(XS) and 0 <= jj < len(YS)) or rows[jj][ii] == '#':
                        continue
                    if dj and vertical[min(j,jj)][i] == '0':
                        continue
                    if di and horizontal is not None and horizontal[j][min(i,ii)] == '0':
                        continue
                    q = (XS[ii],YS[jj])
                    cost = abs(q[0]-x)/2.5 + abs(q[1]-y)/3.5
                    edges.append((q,action,cost))
                self.graph[p] = edges
        # Side tunnels join the left and right borders.
        for y in tunnels:
            a,b = (18,y),(158,y)
            self.graph[a].append((b,3,8.0)); self.graph[b].append((a,2,8.0))
        center_rows = (2,26,50,98,122,146) if maze_type == 3 else (2,26,50,98,122,158)
        for y in center_rows:
            base = 59 + 3 * YS.index(y)
            self.pellet_bits.extend((((88,y), base+1, 64), ((88,y), base+2, 64)))

    def reset(self):
        if self.maze_type != 0:
            self.load_maze(0)
        self.prev = None
        self.heading = 3
        self.action = 3
        self.last_lives = 3
        self.still = 0
        self.decision = None
        self.prev_dot_count = None
        self.steps = 0
        self.prev_ghosts = None
        self.prev_flags = None
        self.ghost_dir = [None]*4
        self.eyes = [False]*4
        self.last_reverse = -100
        self.occupied = set()

    def nearest(self, x, y):
        return min(self.graph, key=lambda p: abs(p[0]-x)+abs(p[1]-y))

    def active_ghosts(self, obs):
        """Ghosts that can kill us: not frightened, not eyes, not in the house."""
        frightened = frightened_timer(obs) > 8
        for j in range(4):
            if (frightened and is_frightened(obs, j)) or self.eyes[j]:
                continue
            x, y = ghost_pos(obs, j)
            if not in_house(x, y):
                yield j, x, y

    def ghost_distances(self, obs, house=False):
        # Dijkstra gives distances along corridors rather than through walls.
        dist = {}
        heap = []
        occupied = self.occupied = set()
        def seed(p, d):
            if d < dist.get(p, 1e9):
                dist[p] = d
                heapq.heappush(heap,(d,p))
        for j, x, y in self.active_ghosts(obs):
            if not on_screen(x, y):
                continue
            ahead = behind = None
            if self.ghost_dir[j] is not None:
                gdx, gdy = self.ghost_dir[j]
                scale = 2.5 if gdx else 3.5
                for p in self.graph:
                    along, cross = offsets(x, y, gdx, gdy, *p)
                    if cross > 3 or abs(along) > 26:
                        continue
                    if along >= 0:
                        if ahead is None or along < ahead[0]:
                            ahead = (along, p)
                    elif behind is None or along > behind[0]:
                        behind = (along, p)
            if ahead is not None:
                # Ghosts rarely reverse, so the node behind is reached late.
                seed(ahead[1], ahead[0]/scale)
                if behind is not None:
                    seed(behind[1], -behind[0]/scale + GHOST_REVERSE_PENALTY)
                    # Walking this edge against the ghost meets it head-on,
                    # whatever the arrival times at the two end nodes say.
                    if ahead[0] > 0:
                        occupied.add((ahead[1], behind[1]))
            else:
                p = self.nearest(x,y)
                seed(p, abs(p[0]-x)/2.5 + abs(p[1]-y)/3.5)
        if house:
            # A ghost in the upper part of the house is on its way out through
            # the door above it and will appear at the door node shortly.
            frightened = frightened_timer(obs) > 8
            door = self.nearest(88, 50)
            for j in range(4):
                x, y = ghost_pos(obs, j)
                if (in_house(x, y) and y <= HOUSE_EXIT_Y and not self.eyes[j]
                        and not (frightened and is_frightened(obs, j))):
                    seed(door, abs(door[1]-y)/3.5 + abs(door[0]-x)/2.5)
        while heap:
            d,p = heapq.heappop(heap)
            if d != dist[p] or d > GHOST_HORIZON:
                continue
            for q,_,c in self.graph[p]:
                nd=d+c
                if nd < dist.get(q,1e9) and nd <= GHOST_HORIZON:
                    dist[q]=nd; heapq.heappush(heap,(nd,q))
        return dist

    def has_escape(self, start, q, cost, danger, powers=(), dots=(), pursued=False):
        """Can we get from start through exit q to a node no ghost reaches first?

        Our arrival time at each node must beat the ghost-distance estimate by
        ESCAPE_MARGIN. Normally an out-of-horizon node or ESCAPE_DEPTH steps
        of travel is enough; when pursued, require 20 steps of travel. A
        reachable power pellet also counts as an escape.
        """
        occupied = self.occupied
        if (start, q) in occupied:
            return False
        best = {start: 0.0}
        # Eating dots slows us down, so a following ghost gains on us.
        if q in dots:
            cost *= 1 + DOT_SLOW
        heap = [(cost, q)]
        while heap:
            t, p = heapq.heappop(heap)
            if t >= best.get(p, 1e9):
                continue
            g = danger.get(p)
            if g is not None and t + ESCAPE_MARGIN > g:
                continue
            best[p] = t
            # A close pursuer can follow through several turns, so look past
            # the first apparently clear node before calling that route safe.
            if ((g is None and not pursued) or t >= (20 if pursued else ESCAPE_DEPTH)
                    or p in powers):
                return True
            for r, _, c in self.graph[p]:
                if (p, r) in occupied:
                    continue
                if r in dots:
                    c *= 1 + DOT_SLOW
                if t + c < best.get(r, 1e9):
                    heapq.heappush(heap, (t + c, r))
        return False

    def safe_exits(self, start, danger, powers=(), dots=(), pursued=False):
        safe = {a for q, a, c in self.graph[start]
                if self.has_escape(start, q, c, danger, powers, dots, pursued)}
        return safe if safe else None

    def search(self, start, heading, danger, avoid, cooldown, allowed=None):
        """Ghost-aware Dijkstra from start; yields (cost, node, first action)."""
        def risk(node):
            g = danger.get(node, 100)
            return max(0, RISK_RADIUS-g)**2 * 1.8 + (AVOID_COST if node in avoid else 0)
        heap=[]
        best={}
        occupied = self.occupied
        for q, action, cost in self.graph[start]:
            if allowed is not None and action not in allowed:
                continue
            turn = 0 if action == heading else TURN_COST
            if action == REVERSE.get(heading):
                turn += REV_COST
                # Avoid dithering: a recent reversal is not undone lightly.
                if cooldown and self.steps - self.last_reverse <= REV_COOLDOWN:
                    turn += REV_COOLDOWN_COST
            total = cost+turn+risk(q)
            if (start, q) in occupied:
                total += OCCUPIED_COST
            if total < best.get(q,1e9):
                best[q]=total; heapq.heappush(heap,(total,q,action))
        while heap:
            d,p,first = heapq.heappop(heap)
            if d != best[p]: continue
            yield d, p, first
            for q,_,cost in self.graph[p]:
                nd=d+cost+risk(q)
                if (p, q) in occupied:
                    nd += OCCUPIED_COST
                if nd < best.get(q,1e9):
                    best[q]=nd; heapq.heappush(heap,(nd,q,first))

    def choose(self, start, heading, pellets, danger, avoid=(), fruit=None, allowed=None):
        # Remember the nearest pellet while looking for a short, low-risk
        # route to the moving fruit. Fall back if the detour is too costly.
        pellet_choice = None
        pellet_cost = 1e9
        for d, p, first in self.search(start, heading, danger, avoid, True, allowed):
            if d > min(22, pellet_cost + 12) and pellet_choice is not None:
                return pellet_choice
            if fruit is not None and p == fruit and d <= 22:
                return first
            if p in pellets and pellet_choice is None:
                if fruit is None:
                    return first
                pellet_choice, pellet_cost = first, d
        # If no pellets remain, continue exploring.
        if pellet_choice is not None:
            return pellet_choice
        if allowed:
            return min(allowed)
        return self.graph[start][0][1] if self.graph[start] else heading

    def hunt(self, start, heading, obs, danger, avoid):
        # Frightened ghosts are worth 200-1600 points; chase one that we can
        # reach well before the frightened timer (one tick per two steps) ends.
        timer = frightened_timer(obs)
        if timer <= HUNT_MIN_TIMER:
            return None
        prey = set()
        for j in range(4):
            gx, gy = ghost_pos(obs, j)
            if is_frightened(obs, j) and not in_house(gx, gy) and on_screen(gx, gy):
                prey.add(self.nearest(gx, gy))
        if not prey or start in prey:
            return None
        limit = HUNT_BUDGET * 2 * (timer - HUNT_MIN_TIMER)
        for d, p, first in self.search(start, heading, danger, avoid, False):
            if d > limit:
                return None
            if p in prey:
                return first
        return None

    def escape_exit(self, p, choice, danger):
        # When the planned exit leads straight into a ghost, take a safer
        # non-reversing exit even if it postpones the nearest dot.
        exits = [(danger.get(q, 100), a) for q, a, _ in self.graph[p]]
        planned = next((d for d, a in exits if a == choice), 100)
        if exits:
            safe, escape = max(exits)
            if planned < 6 and safe > 8 and safe > planned + 5 and escape != REVERSE[self.heading]:
                return escape
        return choice

    def head_on_threat(self, obs, x, y):
        # A ghost approaching head-on in our corridor, or entering the
        # junction just ahead from a side, can collide between decisions.
        # Reverse only if the corridor behind us is clear.
        dx, dy = DIRS[self.heading]
        ahead = False
        for j, gx, gy in self.active_ghosts(obs):
            along, cross = offsets(x, y, dx, dy, gx, gy)
            if cross > 3:
                continue
            if -30 <= along < 0:
                # A distant ghost moving away behind us is not an immediate
                # obstacle to a reversal; a close or closing ghost still is.
                px, py = self.prev_ghosts[j]
                moving = (gx-px)*dx + (gy-py)*dy
                if along >= -10 or moving >= 0:
                    return False
                continue
            if not 0 < along <= 24:
                continue
            if frightened_timer(obs) and is_frightened(obs, j):
                continue
            px, py = self.prev_ghosts[j]
            moving = (gx-px)*dx + (gy-py)*dy
            if moving < 0:
                ahead = True
            elif moving == 0 and along <= 12:
                for node in self.graph:
                    node_along, node_cross = offsets(x, y, dx, dy, *node)
                    nx, ny = node
                    if (len(self.graph[node]) >= 3
                            and 0 < node_along <= 12 and node_cross <= 2
                            and abs(gx-nx) + abs(gy-ny) <= 4
                            and abs(px-nx) + abs(py-ny) > abs(gx-nx) + abs(gy-ny)):
                        ahead = True
                        break
        return ahead

    def update_tracking(self, obs, x, y, lives):
        self.steps += 1
        if lives < self.last_lives:
            # All ghosts respawn after a life loss, including the one outside
            # the house, so none of the previous eyes remain harmless.
            self.eyes = [False]*4
            self.prev = None
            self.heading = self.action = 3
            self.decision = None
        self.last_lives = lives
        # A frightened ghost that loses its frightened bit while the timer is
        # still running has been eaten: its eyes return home and are harmless.
        timer = frightened_timer(obs)
        flags = [int(obs[1+j]) for j in range(4)]
        for j in range(4):
            gx, gy = ghost_pos(obs, j)
            if self.prev_flags is not None and timer > 2:
                if self.prev_flags[j] & 128 and not flags[j] & 128:
                    self.eyes[j] = True
            if self.eyes[j] and (in_house(gx, gy) or flags[j] & 128):
                self.eyes[j] = False
        self.prev_flags = flags
        # Each ghost's direction of travel since the previous frame.
        if self.prev_ghosts is not None:
            for j in range(4):
                gx, gy = ghost_pos(obs, j)
                px, py = self.prev_ghosts[j]
                mx, my = gx-px, gy-py
                if abs(mx) > 20 or abs(my) > 20:
                    self.ghost_dir[j] = None
                elif mx or my:
                    self.ghost_dir[j] = ((1 if mx > 0 else -1), 0) if abs(mx) > abs(my) else (0, (1 if my > 0 else -1))
        # Our own heading; tunnel wraps count as one step.
        if self.prev is not None:
            dx,dy=x-self.prev[0],y-self.prev[1]
            if abs(dx)>100: dx = -1 if dx>0 else 1
            if abs(dx)>0 or abs(dy)>0:
                self.heading = (2 if dx>0 else 3) if abs(dx)>abs(dy) else (4 if dy>0 else 1)
                self.still=0
            else:
                self.still += 1
        self.prev=(x,y)

    def decide(self, obs, p, x, y, powers, dots):
        danger = self.ghost_distances(obs)
        # Fruit moves through the maze and is worth much more on
        # later boards. Earlier fruit is pursued only when very close.
        fruit = None
        fx, fy = int(obs[11]), int(obs[17])
        if (on_screen(fx, fy)
                and abs(fx-x) + abs(fy-y) <= (40 if self.maze_type >= 2 else FRUIT_EARLY)):
            target = self.nearest(fx, fy)
            if target != p:
                fruit = target
        # Save power pellets until a ghost is close enough to be
        # worth eating, rather than wasting them on an empty maze.
        targets = powers | dots
        avoid = ()
        if (powers and dots and (frightened_timer(obs) > 8
                                 or danger.get(p, 100) >= POWER_TRIGGER)):
            targets = dots
            avoid = powers
        choice = self.hunt(p, self.heading, obs, danger, avoid)
        if choice is None:
            choice = self.choose(p, self.heading, targets, danger, avoid, fruit)
        choice = self.escape_exit(p, choice, danger)
        # Do not walk into a pocket that the ghosts can close off: if another
        # exit still has a way out, plan within those exits. Ghosts about to
        # leave the house count here but not in the route risk (too timid).
        dx, dy = DIRS[self.heading]
        pursued = any(-18 <= along < 0 and cross <= 3
                      for _, gx, gy in self.active_ghosts(obs)
                      for along, cross in [offsets(x, y, dx, dy, gx, gy)])
        safe = self.safe_exits(p, self.ghost_distances(obs, True), powers, dots, pursued)
        if safe is not None and choice not in safe:
            choice = self.choose(p, self.heading, targets, danger, avoid, fruit, safe)
        return choice

    def act(self, obs, info):
        maze_type = min(int(obs[0]), 3)
        if maze_type != self.maze_type:
            self.load_maze(maze_type)
            self.eyes = [False]*4
            self.decision = None
            self.prev_dot_count = None
        x,y = int(obs[10]),int(obs[16])
        self.update_tracking(obs, x, y, int(info.get('lives',3)))
        # Re-read dot flags rather than guessing consumption from position.
        powers = {p for p,bit in POWER_BITS.items() if int(obs[117]) & bit}
        dots = {p for p, i, bit in self.pellet_bits if int(obs[i]) & bit}
        if self.prev_dot_count is not None and len(dots) > self.prev_dot_count + 20:
            self.eyes = [False]*4
            self.decision = None   # a new board started
        self.prev_dot_count = len(dots)
        # Decide at the next graph point, early enough to buffer a turn.
        dx,dy=DIRS[self.heading]
        candidates=[]
        for p in self.graph:
            along, cross = offsets(x, y, dx, dy, *p)
            if cross <= 2 and -0.1 <= along <= 4:
                candidates.append((along,p))
        if candidates:
            p = min(candidates)[1]
            key=(p,self.heading)
            if key != self.decision or self.still >= 3:
                choice = self.decide(obs, p, x, y, powers, dots)
                if choice == REVERSE[self.heading]:
                    self.last_reverse = self.steps
                self.action = choice
                self.decision = key
                self.still=0
        elif self.still >= 3:
            p=self.nearest(x,y)
            self.action=self.choose(p,self.heading,powers | dots,self.ghost_distances(obs))
            self.decision=(p,self.heading)
            self.still=0
        if (self.action == self.heading and self.prev_ghosts is not None
                and self.head_on_threat(obs, x, y)):
            self.action = REVERSE[self.heading]
            self.decision = None
            self.last_reverse = self.steps
        self.prev_ghosts = [ghost_pos(obs, j) for j in range(4)]
        return self.action

Montezuma's Revenge · sticky actions

sticky-action champion, generation 6 (mostly Codex, one Claude Code generation) · dev 53,369 (start 3,441; human 4,753); generation 7 has since reached 80,184 · 1,724 lines of Python

  • No exploration bonus and no search: a scripted room-by-room route through three levels, a state machine whose steps advance on RAM checks (room, position, movement state, inventory, lives).
  • Found a laser and bridge countdown in RAM and crosses laser gates and disappearing bridges on it; jumps the skull and spiders on their live position and direction.
  • Budgets lives: skips some prizes and takes shorter paths when few lives remain.
  • For sticky actions, steps that used to be fixed step counts now wait for what RAM shows: a jump is not done until the player is seen in the air, and a missed key is retried while its flag is still set.
  • Jumps over snakes and enemies from standing, inside measured take-off windows, because a repeated input only delays a standing jump but can carry a running jump forward.
  • After a death almost anywhere on the route it waits for the respawn and retries that section; if a repeated input carries it past a ladder, it steps back.

def standing_jump(x, lo, hi, movement, rightward):
    """Step into lo <= x <= hi, then jump from standing; None unless standing.

    A sticky repeat only delays a standing jump in place, whereas it can
    shift a running jump's take-off by a step.
    """
    if movement == 18:  # still settling after a landing
        return WAIT
    if movement != 8:
        return None
    if lo <= x <= hi:
        return JUMP_RIGHT if rightward else JUMP_LEFT
    if rightward:
        return RIGHT if x < lo else LEFT
    return LEFT if x > hi else RIGHT


def climb_from_respawn(x, y, movement):
    """WAIT while dying, then climb a central ladder to its floor; else None."""
    if movement in FALLING:
        return WAIT
    if x == 77 and y != 235:
        return UP if y < 235 else DOWN
    return None
